title: Python: R4, a local whose every binding is Cls(...) of one class resolves its method calls (DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group R4, verbatim: 'R4, every binding of a local is Cls(...) of one class: admitted under item 2, with the nonlocal proviso.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; for a local, writes through nonlocal in nested scopes count as bindings. Second in the DEC-303 (a23) build order after M1 (R4, ALIAS, TS, Q1, (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. Per (a23) item 1 the item-3 group sizes are re-derived on the fixed baseline. Interaction with (a25) (a later task): a write to x.m on a local x bound under R4 or E1 makes x.m() unresolved; not built here. Lessons from K1, LIT and M1 to apply before the first push: enumerate every way the name can get a second binding in EVERY module the rule reads (the scope, any nested scope through nonlocal, and any module a constructor import passes through), give each its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the receiver bin, count bindings with enumerableBindings (never S3 localNames), refuse module-level stars, and read stars, globals, class bodies and annotations. Existing 6d knownClassOf and E1 resolve an imported or dotted constructor by qualname with source-module bindings uncounted (named follow-up; R4 must not widen that gap).

acceptanceCriteria.text: a local whose EVERY binding in its scope is a call Cls(...) of one and the same in-repo class (two or more such bindings allowed, nothing else) resolves a method call on it to that class method, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins; the class must pass the same checks as the 6d known-class local case and E1 (MRO ok, no __new__, no metaclass, no opaque base, no replacing decorator)

each of these leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the call stays in its current bin (bin delta against the same file without the rule): any binding of the local that is not Cls(...) of that class (a different class, a factory, a literal, a parameter, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, augmented, annotated, tuple or star target, type alias); an enumerated binding that cannot be read; a nonlocal write from a nested scope (def or lambda, at any depth) that binds the name to anything but Cls(...) of the same class, and a nonlocal binding in a nested scope counted as a binding of the local; a global declaration of the name in the scope; a class-body or comprehension scope reading; a constructor that is a dotted name, an imported name whose source module has a second binding, a factory, an external class; all bindings counting through the shared enumeration (enumerableBindings), never S3 localNames

each rule has a mutation check that goes red (mutants listed by name, equivalent mutants said so), and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with every in-repo edge it creates or removes named per site and sent to the leader before the clear; no receiver-to-external moves unexplained
